newsitem.title: UK: DBS Management says now received PIA letter.
newsitem.headline: DBS Management says now received PIA letter.

text.p: Business support services group DBS Management Plc said on Monday it now has a letter from the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) indicating they have started disciplinary action against its DBS Financial Management unit.
It said in a statement a further announcement would be made when the process has been completed.
DBS said earlier, in a response to an article in Monday's Independent newspaper, it had "no knowledge" of any fine to be imposed on it by the PIA over alleged pensions mis-selling.
The newspaper had said a 500,000 stg fine -- which would be the largest given by the PIA for a rule breach -- was close to being agreed by the financial services regulator.
In its earlier statement, DBS said that while it did not know of any fine it "considers its resources are adequate to cover such a penalty in the event of it being confirmed".
Shares in DBS, which had initially eased 27-1/2 pence this morning, fell further on the latest statement and were down 80 pence at 1,165 pence at 1300 GMT.

DBS earlier confirmed its commitment to ensure that any investors who bought personal pensions through its members are properly dealt with under the terms of the pensions review by financial watchdog the Securities and Investments Board (SIB).
It said it has made "substantial" provisions to cover the costs of accelerating the review.
The Independent said the fine would be an embarrassment to DBS chairman Ken Davy, who sits on the PIA board.
